This is a platform administration and control role, not a solution development role. The AI Administrator is not expected to build AI applications or agents; AI and Automation Engineers build and evaluate solutions, and AI Business Liaisons qualify opportunities and support adoption. The Administrator ensures that AI capabilities move from prototype through pilot and production with appropriate access, data protection, logging, and cost visibility, and that TRI can produce evidence of these controls for client, ISO 27001, and federal (e.g., FISMA/NIST) security reviews. Job Requirements Experience administering Microsoft Azure, including subscriptions, resource groups, Azure RBAC, networking, Key Vault, and monitoring. Experience implementing least-privilege and privileged access controls, preferably with Entra Privileged Identity Management and access reviews. Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 security and compliance administration, including Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels, DLP, and audit. Scripting and automation with PowerShell, Azure CLI, and/or Microsoft Graph. Microsoft certifications such as AZ-104, AZ-500, SC-300, SC-401, or AI-102. Federal contracting, clinical research, life sciences, or regulated/validated environment experience. Experience supporting FISMA, FedRAMP, CMMC, or ISO 27001 assessments and audits. Experience helping establish an AI governance, AI Center of Excellence, or AI platform operating model. Experience building SIEM detections or monitoring use cases specific to AI and agent activity. Demonstrated ability to tune guardrails and DLP controls to protect data without disrupting legitimate business and project work. This role is fully remote for those living in the DMV area. (Maryland, Virginia, Washington D.C.)
